clue.text: Northern supporter runs with promise to deliver port in the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the word for the supporter is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an oath is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: Someone up north promises to deliver something, with a supporter in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern' turns BRA upward to give ARB. 'to deliver' is a link: the pieces deliver the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbroath is a harbour town on the east coast of Scotland, famous for its smoked haddock.

clue.text: Empty place south of Muswell Hill, say — used, vacated housing

indicators.note: housing means the outside letters hold the rest within them
vacated means the word is emptied of its middle, keeping only its ends
in a down clue, south of puts this piece below the postcode

parts.note: Muswell Hill is a London district with the postcode N10, written N TEN
to ante is to place a stake before a hand of poker

explanation.surface: An empty property near Muswell Hill, previously used, now vacated.
explanation.walkthrough: Muswell Hill, a north London suburb, has the postcode N10, read as N + TEN. ANTE goes under it, and both sit inside U...D, the ends left when 'used' is 'vacated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with no tenants living in it is empty.

clue.text: Display map that initially shows life form not seen on earth?

definitions.text: life form not seen on earth?

parts.note: to air something is to display or show it publicly
a plan is a map or diagram

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone shows a map that seems to reveal an alien life form.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like an alien, but 'not seen on earth' means not grown in soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Epiphytes like these take moisture from the atmosphere and grow on trees, never in the ground.

clue.text: Off-colour pants, say, squashing two articles

indicators.note: squashing means the underwear holds the other letters pressed inside it
two says the article goes in twice, each copy at a separate place inside the pants

parts.note: pants are an example of underwear
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone's pants look discoloured, with a couple of items crushed together.
explanation.walkthrough: The two THEs go in separately: UNDER + THE + WEA + THE + R.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly ill is the idiomatic sense of being off-colour.

clue.text: Perhaps Spielberg's heartless conjecture about one of his films being rejected

definitions.note: Steven Spielberg is an example; the 's is 'is', a link

indicators.note: about means the outer letters surround the film's title
heartless means the middle letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: to augur is to foretell or conjecture

indicators.note: being rejected means the film's title is turned back to front

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film about an alien

explanation.surface: A guess that one of Spielberg's films was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conjecture' here is a verb, matching the verb augur. 'Spielberg's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A film director with a distinctive personal style is called an auteur, as Spielberg is often described.

clue.text: Circus attraction in London aching to travel north

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading the word from the bottom up

parts.note: sore means aching

explanation.surface: An aching visitor heads north from a London circus.
explanation.walkthrough: Circus here is Piccadilly Circus, a road junction in London, not a big top.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue at Piccadilly Circus is popularly named after the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Stuff found between coupled identical proteins

indicators.note: found between two coupled copies means the letters straddle the join, so the end of the protein word comes round to the front

parts.note: gluten is a mixture of proteins found in wheat

explanation.surface: Something stuffed between two matching proteins, like a sandwich filling.
explanation.walkthrough: Write GLUTEN GLUTEN; the answer spans the join, the same as moving EN to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut or cram is to stuff, and the archaic verb means to gorge or fill up.

clue.text: British campaign that is backing oil producers

definitions.note: plural for a country taken as its oil industry

parts.note: to run is to campaign for office

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A British campaign backing oil producers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sultanate on Borneo is wealthy chiefly from its oil and gas reserves.

clue.text: No charge for this on iTunes, unlimited or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters are arranged in another way
unlimited means the phrase loses its limits, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A free download on iTunes, with or without limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips O and S from ON ITUNES, leaving NITUNE; add OR and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle carries zero electric charge.

clue.text: Cheese crisp? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: brief means crisp or concise

explanation.surface: Is that cheese crisp? Not really.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese named after the region east of Paris.

clue.text: Grasping penis here, left aroused

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A deliberately risqué picture of sexual arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail or limb able to grip objects, like a monkey's, is described this way.

clue.text: Finish off nuts and fruit

indicators.note: finish off means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: bananas is slang for nuts or crazy

explanation.surface: A snack of nuts and fruit, polished off.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curved tropical fruit with yellow skin.

clue.text: Become keen on act

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B places A after B

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act
being into something means being keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone grows enthusiastic about a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To change into something else is to become it.

clue.text: Shot in air raid, regularly going down

indicators.note: regularly means every second letter is taken

parts.note: a descent is a going down

explanation.surface: Someone shot down during an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a gunshot, but shot silk changes colour in the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that shows shifting colours, like shot silk, is described with this word.

clue.text: Is debate with hag about question regarding affairs of state? Au contraire

definitions.text: question regarding affairs of state? Au contraire

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A political debate with a hag, about matters of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Au contraire' flips 'affairs of state' to 'state of affairs': the answer asks what is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: An indignant query demanding to know the reason for a situation or someone's behaviour.

clue.text: Country connection having long lost item in the Camp David drawing room?

definitions.text: item in the Camp David drawing room?

parts.note: India is a country

indicators.note: lost means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A link to a country, lost at the presidential retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Camp David sounds like the US presidential retreat, but here 'camp' describes a flamboyant artist named David.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense black ink used for drawing would be found in an artist's studio.

clue.text: Decorate Nobleman with head turned around?

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about
the first letter, turned on its side, becomes a different letter shape

explanation.surface: Honouring a nobleman whose head is turned.
explanation.walkthrough: N rotated a quarter turn looks like Z, so ZOBLEMAN, rearranged, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To emblazon is to adorn conspicuously, as with heraldic devices.

clue.text: Toxic plant manufacture also reactive, initially contained

indicators.note: contained means the other letters are held within the word

parts.note: to make is to manufacture
and means also

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A dangerous plant is processed, its reactive substances held in check.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous Mediterranean herb with a forked root, steeped in folklore.

clue.text: Bore outdoor gear

definitions.meaning: a dull obsessive person, a nerd

explanation.surface: A boring person in hiking gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a tedious enthusiast and a weatherproof jacket go by this word.

clue.text: Climb, emerging topless

indicators.note: in a down clue, topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: nascent means emerging or just coming into being

explanation.surface: Climbing out without a top on.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb up a mountain or slope.

clue.text: Drug taken by radio host with gong and drum

indicators.note: taken by places the drug after the host who takes it

parts.note: a DJ is a disc jockey hosting a radio show
E is short for ecstasy
an MBE is an honour, informally a gong

explanation.surface: A radio DJ on drugs with a gong and a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' looks like a percussion instrument beside the drum, but it is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet-shaped West African hand drum.

clue.text: Resident of 1 caught between road and river going round foreign peninsula

indicators.note: caught between means this piece sits between the road and the river
going round means the road and river letters are turned back to front

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest road, written AI
the Avon is a river in England
Arbroath, the answer at 1, is in Scotland, so its resident is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scotsman caught between a road and a river abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to the answer at 1-down, a Scottish town, so its resident is a Scot. The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write it AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian province consisting mostly of a peninsula on the Atlantic.

clue.text: Run out of caustic chemical

indicators.note: out of means the letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: acrid means harsh or caustic
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Running out of a caustic chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caustic chemical' reads as one phrase, but caustic is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrosive substance with a pH below seven is a chemical.

clue.text: See you around food that's picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: Goodbye, said around the food that has been collected.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian farewell borrowed into casual English.

clue.text: Endurance game

definitions.meaning: the ability to put up with delay or trouble calmly
a card game for one player, also called solitaire

explanation.surface: A game of endurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both calm forbearance and a solo card game go by this word.

clue.text: Big bird's eggs found by gate — that's logical

indicators.note: found by places the eggs next to the gate, after it

parts.note: a NAND gate is a logic gate in electronics
an O looks like an egg, so two eggs are OO

explanation.surface: A large bird's eggs turn up beside a gate, which makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's logical' reads as comment, but it makes the gate a logic gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea, a large flightless South American bird, is also called by this name.
